subject: Agriculture
title: Biochar
description: A micro-lesson that makes Biochar usable.

hook.text: Amazonian farmers created super-fertile 'terra preta' soil 2,000 years ago using charcoal. We're rediscovering their trick.

buildup.text: Biochar is charcoal made by heating organic matter without oxygen. Its porous structure persists for centuries.

discovery.text: Biochar improves water retention, nutrient holding, and microbial habitat—especially in poor, sandy soils.

twist.text: The carbon in biochar is locked away for hundreds of years—it's a permanent form of carbon sequestration.

climax.text: Scaling biochar remains challenging—production costs are high and benefits vary dramatically by soil type.

punchline.text: Ancient Amazonians solved carbon storage 2,000 years ago. We're just catching up.

quiz.question: What is terra preta?
options: Super-fertile Amazonian soil created with charcoal by ancient farmers
